The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet no.07/2011 and charge sheet no.07A/2011 as well as the entire proceedings of S.T. No.761/2011 arising out of Case Crime No.198/2011, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Thakurganj,
District-Lucknow, pending before the court of A.D.J. Court No.7, Lucknow on the basis of compromise.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the complainant is mother of the deceased, who is nearly 75 years old and the child born out of wedlock of the petitioner no.1; Dilip Kashyap and daughter of opposite party no.2, who is nearly 14 years, is with the opposite party no.2.
She is not in a position to take care of the aforesaid child, therefore, she is ready and willing to amicable settle the disputes by entering into compromise.

In this regard, a compromise deed on behalf of the both the parties has been filed before the court concerned stating therein that they do not want to proceed with the case, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexure No.2 to this application.
In such circumstances, seeing the future of the child, the Court can always compound the offences and record the compromise entered into between the parties quashing the proceedings in such cases.
In support of his contention, he has relied upon the judgment of the Andhra Pradesh High Court passed in Criminal Petition No.378 of 2022 decided on 22.03.2022.
Therefore, no useful purpose would be served in continuing the proceedings before the court below and the same is not only sheer wastage of time of the Court but also abuse of the process of law.
Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as learned AGA does not dispute the aforesaid fact.
In such special circumstances, the Court can always compound the offences and record the compromise entered into between the parties quashing the proceedings in such cases.

It would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding.
In view of the above, both the parties are directed to appear before the court below along with copy of compromise deed as well as a certified copy of this order within two weeks from today.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law,
as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two months from today.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the concerned court shall also record the statement of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not?

The court in that scenario will allow the parties to obtain certified copy of the report as well as compromise and it will be open to the applicants to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.
Till verification of compromise between the parties by the court concerned, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
With the aforesaid directions, this application is finally disposed of.

Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Jitendra/-
